report.answer_text:
John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis shared the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics “for the discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit.” (nobelprize.org)
Their experiments showed that a superconducting circuit large enough to hold in your hand could tunnel through an energy barrier it couldn’t cross according to classical physics, and that it had discrete energy levels. (nobelprize.org)

quotes.text: This year’s Nobel Prize Laureates conducted experiments with an electrical circuit in which they demonstrated both quantum mechanical tunnelling and quantised energy levels in a system big enough to be held in the hand.
In the experiment the system shows its quantum character by managing to escape the zerovoltage state through tunnelling.
The system is trapped in this state, as if behind a barrier that it cannot cross.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state the circuit was big enough to be held in the hand, that it escaped the zero-voltage state by quantum tunnelling, and that it was trapped behind a barrier it cannot cross, which together back every fact in the claim.
pages.page_reason: The page states the laureates demonstrated quantum tunnelling in an electrical circuit big enough to be held in the hand, with a macroscopic superconducting system escaping a zero-voltage state trapped behind a barrier it cannot cross, which matches the claim's substance.
